You are an expert bioinformatician.
Explain the biochemical interaction and molecular mechanism between the drug 'Lapatinib', the biological target 'ERBB2', and the pathological condition 'HER2-positive Breast Cancer'.
Detail the specific binding mechanism, affinity, and clinical therapeutic rationale.
Be specific and concise (3-5 sentences).
text: Lapatinib is a small-molecule, ATP-competitive dual tyrosine kinase inhibitor that binds reversibly to the intracellular kinase domain of ERBB2 (HER2), selectively stabilizing an inactive conformation of the receptor with a high binding affinity ($K_i \approx 13 \text{ nM}$). By occupying the ATP-binding pocket, Lapatinib blocks autophosphorylation and prevents downstream activation of the oncogenic MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling pathways that drive cell proliferation and survival. In HER2-positive breast cancer—a subtype characterized by *ERBB2* gene amplification and receptor overexpression—this targeted enzymatic inhibition triggers apoptosis and arrests cell cycle progression. Therapeutically, Lapatinib’s unique ability to cross the blood-brain barrier makes it clinically effective in treating HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, particularly in patients who have developed brain metastases or resistance to domain-targeting antibody therapies like trastuzumab.
